Subject: Pilot readiness: Chartwell — technical acceptance & pilot scope

Hi Elena / Tom —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from my side and concrete asks so we can get engineering onboarded next week. I kept this focused on the technical acceptance criteria we discussed plus the initial pilot scope.

Key pain / goal summary
- Pain: current retrieval/rerank pipeline has 1.2s average response and inconsistent context handling for multi-turn summaries.
- Goal: reduce 90/95p latency to <200ms for interactive assistant flows while improving top-1 relevance via embeddings + rerank for doc search.
- Volume: expected pilot steady-state ~8–12k requests/day with bursts to 25k/day for two weeks.

Fit & recommended Redwood approach
- Model/infra: host a light LLM variant for interactive queries + dedicated rerank model for embedding similarity. Quantized model suggested for cost control.
- Function calling / structured output: we'll use function calling to return a strict JSON schema for entity extraction and actionability (see example schema we demoed).
- Streaming + fallback: enable streaming for UI responsiveness; add a short-token non-streaming fallback for clients that can't handle streams.
- Caching: prefix/KV caching for repeated conversational context to reduce token cost on long threads.
- Batching: target small continuous batches (size 4–8) for throughput without breaking latency SLOs.

Security & compliance asks
- SOC2 attestation and evidence for audit — we can provide our attestation and SOC-related docs.
- Option for VPC peering or private deployment if you require network isolation (Pilot can start on Hosted w/ dedicated tenancy).
- Token auth: service-account-based tokens and short-lived creds for client SDKs.

Acceptance criteria (technical) — must-haves to sign-off pilot readiness
1) SDK integration: Chartwell devs can call Redwood SDK to stream partial responses and receive function-call structured JSON (example schema roundtrip).
2) Latency: end-to-end p95 <= 250ms on interactive flows in pilot environment (we'll aim for 150ms but set 250ms as threshold).
3) Relevance: rerank improves top-1 precision by >= 12% on your gold set (you'll provide an evaluation set or we can use a small shared prompt set).
4) Security: SOC2 attestation delivered and initial security questionnaire answered.

Next steps (owners & rough ETA)
- Redwood to deliver: SOC2 attestation PDF + sample function-calling SDK patch (Sergio) — ETA: 2026-07-16
- Redwood eng (Priyom) to schedule technical onboarding & provide dev sandbox + eval keys — ETA: 2026-07-20
- Chartwell to share: 100–200 eval prompts + a small gold set for rerank comparison, and completed security questionnaire — ETA: 2026-07-19
- Calendar: Proposed 60-min technical onboarding (Priyom + eng) — propose week of 7/20; Sergio will send invite once we lock a slot.

Attachments: redwood-soc2-attestation.pdf (will share), pilot-map-v1.docx (MVP plan).

If anything above needs clarifying, call it out and I’ll adjust. Otherwise I’ll send SOC2 and the function-calling example on Friday.

Thanks,
Sergio
